enquiry: Our juice bottling line sometimes fills batches that customers describe as tasting off. We were told UV/Vis spectroscopy is extremely sensitive, so we want to put it on the filler and let it reject bad batches automatically. We do not know what causes the off taste.

clarification_questions.question: What exactly goes wrong today, how often do off-taste batches occur, and what decision should real-time data drive: stop the filler, divert a batch, or alert an operator?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the decision the sensor must support and whether automatic rejection is needed at all.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pain frequency unknown; the first step is a diagnosis of the off-taste cause before any automatic rejection is designed.

clarification_questions.question: Which compound, property or sensory attribute is associated with the off taste, and do you know whether it is at ppm or % level, or is the cause still unknown?
clarification_questions.why: UV/Vis only detects a defined absorbing species; sensitivity alone does not identify the cause.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Cause unknown; lab screening must first establish whether any UV/Vis-active species correlates with the off taste and at what level.

clarification_questions.question: Which juice product(s) are filled, and is the juice clear, cloudy with pulp or particles, or opaque?
clarification_questions.why: Turbidity and absorbing matrix components determine whether transmission, transflection or ATR geometry is viable.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical properties unknown; treat the juice as possibly turbid and test geometry in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: How does the juice vary between batches (fruit origin, blending, pasteurisation, storage time, CIP or cleaning of the filler), and at what temperature and flow does it pass the measuring point?
clarification_questions.why: Batch variation and cleaning residues can cause optical changes unrelated to taste, which would produce false rejections.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Process variation unknown; lab screening must include representative batches with normal variation.

clarification_questions.question: Where on the filler would the measurement take place, is there a flow-through point with access for a probe, and how far is the analyzer from that point?
clarification_questions.why: Determines probe type, contact possibility and whether the analyzer can sit close to the process.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point unknown; the analyzer is assumed to need a dedicated flow-through measuring point, to be confirmed.

clarification_questions.question: How is off taste assessed today, by sensory panel, lab analysis or both, and how accurate or repeatable is that reference?
clarification_questions.why: Without a reference that defines a bad batch, no optical model can be trained or validated.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method unknown; a sensory or lab reference must be defined and checked for repeatability in the feasibility study.

clarification_questions.question: What are the accuracy, response time and budget requirements, including how many false rejections of good batches are acceptable?
clarification_questions.why: Sets whether a single optical method and a simple sensor are sufficient and what validation is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; no performance is assumed until the expert agrees targets with the client.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The claim says silica fibers suit Raman, but the cited S02 p.6 chart lists silica fibers only for UV-VIS (190-1200 nm) and VIS-NIR (350-2400 nm) and never mentions Raman. The Raman region is stated only on S01 p.5, which is not cited here. Fix: Keep the silica-fiber UV-VIS and VIS-NIR ranges and the IR-fiber point from S02 p.6, and cite S01 p.5 for the Raman spectral region (visible and NIR) instead of attributing a Raman fiber statement to S02 p.6.

not_supported: S01 p.16 says turbidity or opacity can saturate the UV-Vis signal, but it does not mention pulp or temperature effects. It also does not say that the signal can change without any taste change. Fix: Limit the risk to what S01 p.16 supports: turbidity or opacity can saturate or change the optical signal. Add pulp or temperature only with a source page that discusses them.

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR fiber probes and NIR online analysis. It does not discuss juice type, blend changes, or calibration validity. Fix: Cite an AFS page that discusses calibration transfer or model validity for changing sample composition (for example the chemometric model discussion on S01 p.5), or remove the calibration-invalidation claim.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [guidance]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [guidance]
